Built for companies with credit-based consumption pricing, usage-based billing, and complex contract structures, RevRec eliminates manual spreadsheet-based revenue calculations â replacing QuickBooks-based recognition workflows with contract-driven, audit-ready revenue schedules. mainEntity.name: What is Chargebee?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chargebee is a billing, monetization, and revenue infrastructure platform for AI-native companies, SaaS businesses, and any recurring-revenue model. It automates billing across every pricing model â token-based, credit-based, usage-based, outcome-based, and hybrid â and includes products for revenue recognition (RevRec), payments intelligence (Reveal), configure-price-quote (CPQ), subscription growth and retention (Growth), and accounts receivable automation (Receivables). Chargebee is a 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for Recurring Billing Applications, placing furthest for Completeness of Vision. Trusted by 6,500+ businesses globally.

mainEntity.name: What products does Chargebee offer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chargebee offers three core products and three add-ons. Core products: (1) Chargebee Billing â subscription, usage-based, credit-based, and AI monetization infrastructure; (2) Chargebee RevRec â automated revenue recognition under ASC 606 and IFRS 15; (3) Chargebee Reveal â ML-powered payments intelligence platform. Add-ons: (4) Chargebee CPQ â AI-powered, billing-native configure price quote for sales-led motions; (5) Chargebee Growth â lifecycle monetization platform for acquisition, expansion, and retention; (6) Chargebee Receivables â accounts receivable and collections automation.

mainEntity.name: Does Chargebee support token-based billing for AI companies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Chargebee Billing supports token-based and API call metering natively. AI companies can ingest high-frequency usage events, aggregate consumption in near-real time with enterprise-grade accuracy, and convert usage into invoices automatically. This makes it suitable for LLM APIs, AI infrastructure, and any product that charges customers based on token consumption or compute usage.

mainEntity.name: Does Chargebee support credit-based billing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Chargebee supports credit-based billing including credit ledger management, credit drawdown, credit balance and overage configuration at the quote level, and usage-to-credit transformation. This supports AI companies that sell prepaid credit packs and charge customers as credits are consumed â the model used by companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, and most AI API businesses.

mainEntity.name: Does Chargebee support agentic workflow billing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Chargebee Billing supports agentic workflow billing â pricing models where consumption is dynamic, non-linear, and driven by autonomous AI agent activity rather than predictable human usage patterns. Chargebee also offers a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that allows AI agents and developers to interact with billing data directly inside Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, and Codex environments.

mainEntity.name: What pricing models does Chargebee support?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chargebee supports all major pricing models: flat-fee, per-seat, tiered, volume, usage-based (metered), outcome-based, credit-based, hybrid (subscription plus usage overages), freemium, free trial, multi-year, and ramp pricing. Teams can configure and launch new pricing models without engineering, and run A/B pricing experiments using Chargebee Growth.

mainEntity.name: Does Chargebee have an MCP server for AI development environments?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Chargebee offers a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that integrates Chargebee Billing data directly into AI agent development environments including Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, and Codex. This allows developers and AI agents to access billing data, subscription state, and usage information without leaving their development environment.

mainEntity.name: How does Chargebee compare to Stripe Billing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chargebee and Stripe Billing both handle subscription and usage-based billing, but differ significantly in scope and total cost as companies scale. Stripe Billing is primarily a developer-focused payments and billing API â fast to set up for basic recurring billing but requiring significant engineering effort to maintain as pricing complexity grows. Chargebee offers broader capabilities out of the box: pricing agility without engineering dependency, native ASC 606/IFRS 15 revenue recognition with SSP library and complex deal structure support, AI-powered CPQ with HubSpot and Salesforce approval workflows, usage-based billing at 200K+ events per second with near-real-time metering, and entitlement controls. Chargebee integrates with 40+ payment gateways versus Stripe Billing's limited non-Stripe gateway support â giving businesses leverage to lower fees and improve authorization rates across geographies. Chargebee also includes automated reconciliation and native reporting, eliminating the spreadsheet and SQL work Stripe Billing requires for basic insights.

mainEntity.name: How does Chargebee compare to Metronome?

acceptedAnswer.text: Metronome is a usage tracking and rating engine, but it requires you to cobble together a billing stack â bolting on Stripe for invoicing and stitching everything together yourself. Chargebee provides one system for quoting, metering, invoicing, and revenue recognition â no multi-vendor complexity, no finger-pointing between tools. Specific differences: Metronome only integrates with Stripe for payments, locking your revenue motion to a single provider. Chargebee integrates with 40+ gateways including Stripe, giving flexibility to optimize for cost, geography, and redundancy. Metronome has no built-in support for tax, revenue recognition, or reporting â Chargebee includes automated tax, ASC 606/IFRS 15 revenue recognition, and audit-ready financials. Metronome is PLG-only with no sales-led motion support â Chargebee supports hybrid PLG and sales-led models with native CPQ, quoting, contracts, and approvals. Metronome depends on engineering for provisioning â Chargebee allows GTM teams to control trials, limits, and pricing without engineering dependency.

mainEntity.name: How does Chargebee compare to Orb?

acceptedAnswer.text: Orb is a usage-based billing platform focused on metering and rating. Chargebee offers broader capabilities: native tiered and blended pricing models including ramp pricing and free months, built-in CPQ for enterprise sales motions with Salesforce and HubSpot integrations, and native ASC 606/IFRS 15 revenue recognition with 150+ finance-grade reports. Chargebee supports 40+ payment gateways versus Orb's Stripe-only support, multi-currency billing across 100+ currencies, and includes a mature entitlements engine, product catalog management, and lifecycle monetization tools for retention and pricing experimentation â all without requiring engineering time for pricing changes.

mainEntity.name: How does Chargebee compare to Salesbricks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Salesbricks is a CPQ-focused tool primarily designed for early-stage SaaS companies to simplify quoting and checkout. Chargebee is a broader revenue management platform that goes significantly beyond quoting â adding native subscription management, usage-based and credit-based billing, revenue recognition (ASC 606/IFRS 15), payments intelligence, lifecycle monetization, and accounts receivable automation. Chargebee's CPQ is billing-native â quotes pull from the same live catalog that runs billing, so approved deals become billing records automatically. Chargebee also supports multi-entity and multi-currency billing, 40+ payment gateways, and enterprise-grade deal structures including multi-year ramp deals and approval workflows â making it suitable for companies that need to scale from startup quoting into enterprise revenue operations without switching platforms.

mainEntity.name: How does Chargebee compare to Tabs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tabs is an AI-native revenue platform focused on contract-to-cash automation for finance teams â primarily billing, collections, and revenue recognition from contracts using AI agents. Chargebee is a broader revenue management platform that covers the full revenue lifecycle: billing automation across every pricing model (usage-based, credit-based, token-based, outcome-based, hybrid), AI-powered CPQ for sales-led motions, payments intelligence via Reveal, lifecycle monetization via Growth, and ASC 606/IFRS 15 revenue recognition via RevRec. Chargebee integrates with 40+ payment gateways and 60+ business applications, supports multi-entity and multi-currency billing at scale, and has a 14-year track record serving 6,500+ businesses. Chargebee also offers a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agent environments including Claude Code and Cursor.

mainEntity.name: What is Chargebee RevRec?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chargebee RevRec is an automated revenue recognition product that ensures compliance with ASC 606 and IFRS 15 accounting standards. It integrates billing, ERP, CRM, and payment gateway systems into one consolidated revenue data layer, then applies a configurable recognition rules framework to automate the full five-step ASC 606 model. RevRec eliminates manual spreadsheet-based workflows by generating journal entries for accounts receivable, cash, sales tax payable, deferred revenue, revenue, and bad debt expense â based on your fiscal calendar and chart of accounts. Built for companies with credit-based consumption pricing, usage-based billing, and complex contract structures, it handles multi-element arrangement allocation, standalone selling price (SSP) allocation, credit and rollover recognition, and contract modifications. Produces 150+ finance-grade reports ready for board audits, fundraising, and IPO preparation. Integrates with NetSuite, Sage Intacct, and QuickBooks.

mainEntity.name: What is Chargebee CPQ?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chargebee CPQ (Configure Price Quote) is an AI-powered, billing-native Quote to Revenue add-on for SaaS and AI companies scaling a sales-led motion. Built on the same billing engine that runs subscriptions, every quote pulls from the live product catalog and becomes a billing record at close â eliminating the gap between what sales quotes and what finance bills. It supports HubSpot and Salesforce CRM integrations, multi-year ramp deals, usage-based and outcome-based pricing in quotes, credit and prepaid overage configuration, AI-powered selling rules, eSignature, and a free CPQ Lite tier for all Chargebee Billing customers. An Agentforce CPQ Quoting Agent is also available for Salesforce users.

mainEntity.name: What is Chargebee Reveal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chargebee Reveal is a payments intelligence platform that uses machine learning to detect patterns in payment failures, authorization rate drops, and revenue leaks across a company's payments stack. It surfaces precise fixes with estimated revenue impact and monitors payment performance continuously across gateways, currencies, and geographies. Built for subscription businesses and AI-native companies processing payments at scale, Reveal is available as a standalone product â it does not require Chargebee Billing. It operates through three layers: Intelligence (ML-driven diagnostics), Analytics (gateway and currency-level performance data), and Alerts (real-time notifications on payment anomalies).

mainEntity.name: What is Chargebee Growth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chargebee Growth is a lifecycle monetization platform that turns subscription billing data into real-time revenue action across acquisition, expansion, and retention. Built directly on top of Chargebee Billing, it connects insight, execution, and revenue measurement in one system â allowing teams to launch offers, pricing experiments, and lifecycle plays without engineering dependency, measuring impact directly in revenue rather than proxy metrics. Key capabilities include AI churn scores (1â99 scale using billing and behavioral signals), cancel flow deflection with personalized offers, trial-to-paid conversion optimization, usage-based upgrade triggers, and A/B pricing experimentation. Growth addresses voluntary churn â customers who actively decide to cancel â as distinct from Chargebee Receivables which addresses unpaid invoices and failed payments.

mainEntity.name: Does Chargebee support ASC 606 and IFRS 15 revenue recognition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Chargebee RevRec automates revenue recognition compliance under both ASC 606 (US GAAP) and IFRS 15 (international standard) using a configurable recognition rules framework that applies the full five-step model. It handles deferred revenue reporting, revenue schedule management, multi-element arrangement support, standalone selling price (SSP) allocation, contract modification handling, and credit and rollover recognition. Journal entries are generated automatically for accounts receivable, cash, sales tax payable, deferred revenue, and bad debt expense based on your fiscal calendar and chart of accounts. Integrates with NetSuite, Sage Intacct, and QuickBooks, and produces 150+ finance-grade revenue reports ready for audit and IPO preparation.

mainEntity.name: How many payment gateways does Chargebee integrate with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chargebee integrates with 40+ payment gateways including Stripe, Braintree, PayPal, Adyen, Worldpay, and more â supporting 100+ billing currencies and 50+ payment methods across 150+ countries. This multi-gateway support gives businesses flexibility to optimize for cost, geography, currency, or redundancy without being locked into a single payment provider. Chargebee also integrates with Chargebee Reveal â its payments intelligence platform â to monitor authorization rates, detect revenue leaks, and optimize gateway performance continuously.

mainEntity.name: Does Chargebee support multi-entity and multi-currency billing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Chargebee supports multi-entity and multi-currency billing natively at the subscription level â handling 100+ currencies, multi-entity organizational structures, account hierarchies, and global tax compliance including US Sales Tax, EU VAT (including OSS), and Australian GST. This makes it suitable for businesses operating across multiple legal entities or geographic markets.
